outputs.name: SAV run summary per lane and read

renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: lane_read_error
  title: Error rate and Q30 per lane and read
  description: |-
    Each dot is a read of a lane: its colour is the PhiX error rate and its size the share of bases at Q30 or above. It answers which lane and read combinations sequenced well.
    How to read: a large, pale dot is a read with high quality and a low error rate. A small, dark dot is a weak read to compare with the other lanes. Index reads have no PhiX error rate, so their colour is empty.
    Source: https://support-docs.illumina.com/SW/SAV/Content/SW/SAV/Metrics.htm
  kind: dot_plot
  roles:
    cluster: lane_label
    gene: read_label
    mean_expression: error_rate
    frac_expressing: frac_q30

- component: advanced_viz
  id: phasing_scatter
  title: Phasing against prephasing
  description: |-
    Each point is a lane of one read: the phasing rate (horizontal) against the prephasing rate (vertical), coloured by the read. It answers whether the chemistry keeps molecules in step along the read.
    How to read: points near the origin are reads where clusters stay in step. A point that sits far from the others is a lane whose chemistry or flow cell deviates, and it is the one to compare with its Q30 and error rate. Index reads report a phasing and prephasing of 0 in the InterOp summary, so read them as not measured rather than perfect.
    Note: the rates are the values Real-Time Analysis uses, estimated from the first 25 cycles of each read.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median prephasing of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Illumina Interop.
    Source: https://support-docs.illumina.com/SW/SAV/Content/SW/SAV/Metrics.htm
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Phasing (% per cycle)
    y_title: Prephasing (% per cycle)
    legend_pos: bottom
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: phasing
    y: prephasing
    label: lane_label
    color: read_label

- component: figure
  title: PhiX error rate per lane and read
  description: |-
    Each bar is a read of a lane: its error rate measured on the PhiX control. It answers which lanes and reads have the most sequencing errors.
    How to read: compare lanes within the same read. A lane clearly above its neighbours for the same read is the one to inspect for a flow cell or fluidics problem. Lanes without a PhiX spike-in have no bar.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median PhiX error rate of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Illumina Interop.
    Source: https://support-docs.illumina.com/SW/SAV/Content/SW/SAV/Metrics.htm
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: lane_label
    y: error_rate
    color: read_label
    barmode: group
    title: PhiX error rate per lane and read
    labels:
      lane_label: Lane
      error_rate: PhiX error rate (%)
      read_label: Read
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: error_rate

- component: card
  title: Highest error rate
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest PhiX error rate of any lane and read, with the spread across them in the box. It answers how bad the worst part of the run is.
    How to read: a maximum far above the box is one lane or read that needs a look. Compare it with its Q30 share before deciding whether to rerun.
  column: error_rate
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: worst lane and read, with the spread

- component: card
  title: Lowest clusters passing filter
  description: |-
    The hero number is the lowest percentage of clusters passing filter of any lane, with the spread across lanes and reads in the box. It answers whether every lane kept a usable share of its clusters.
    How to read: a low minimum is a lane that was over-clustered or had poor signal, so it gives fewer reads. Check its density next.
    Source: https://support-docs.illumina.com/SW/SAV/Content/SW/SAV/Metrics.htm
  column: pct_cluster_pf
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: lowest lane, with the spread

- component: card
  title: Total yield
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total yield in gigabases over all lanes and reads, with the median and the largest per row next to it, and the bars rank the lanes. It answers how much data the run produced and which lanes carry it.
    How to read: lanes of similar size mean even loading. A short bar is a lane that lost clusters or was not loaded.
    Source: https://support-docs.illumina.com/SW/SAV/Content/SW/SAV/Metrics.htm
  column: yield_gb
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: lane_label
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: yield, by lane

- component: table
  title: Run summary per lane and read
  description: |-
    Each row is a read of a lane: the tiles, density, clusters passing filter, phasing and prephasing, Q30 share, yield and PhiX error rate. It answers the same questions as the Sequencing Analysis Viewer summary tab.
    How to read: sort by error rate or Q30 to find the weakest lane and read.
